exploreItems.title: Date on the card
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The canal opened in 1869; the classroom route task is dated 1870.

exploreItems.title: Connected seas
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Suez links the Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea through Egypt.

exploreItems.title: What changed
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: It provided a shorter Europe-Asia water connection; it did not remove travel costs.

exploreItems.title: 1855: a port opens
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The Iloilo marker dates its opening to international trade to 1855.

exploreItems.title: 1859: sugar goes outward
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The marker records sugar shipped from Iloilo to Melbourne.

exploreItems.title: 1863: machinery comes in
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Sugar-mill machinery arrived from Glasgow; trade moved goods in both directions.

exploreItems.title: Person and place
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Isabelo de los Reyes came from Vigan, Ilocos Sur.

exploreItems.title: Publication and year
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: He founded El Ilocano in 1889.

exploreItems.title: Action
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Publishing requires people to prepare and share written material.

exploreItems.title: Place and action
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Malolos women requested permission for a school in Bulacan.

exploreItems.title: 1888 request
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The marker dates their request to 12 December 1888 and describes their own funding.

exploreItems.title: Initiative and support
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Their request came before Rizal's later letter praising their initiative.

exploreItems.title: Named advocate
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Pedro Pelaez defended the rights of Filipino secular clergy.

exploreItems.title: Documented concern
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Parish transfers and restrictions affected opportunities to administer parishes.

exploreItems.title: Action toward change
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Written objections and arguments supported a reform request; an objection is not proof of its success.

exploreItems.title: Secular
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: In this use, secular clergy are under a bishop and not members of a religious order.

exploreItems.title: Regular
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Regular clergy belong to religious orders. Regular refers to an order's rule.

exploreItems.title: Keep categories distinct
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Clergy category is not the same as religion, nationality or personal worth.

exploreItems.title: Administration
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The secularization dispute concerns who administers parishes.

exploreItems.title: Participation
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Filipinization concerns Filipino priests' participation in parish leadership.

exploreItems.title: Proposed change
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A modern classroom summary asks for fair consideration of qualified clergy; it is not an original decree.

exploreItems.title: Local community
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A parish includes a Catholic community, not only a building.

exploreItems.title: Responsibilities
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A priest serves the parish; administering concerns continuing responsibilities.

exploreItems.title: Wider organization
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A diocese is under a bishop and can include parishes.

exploreItems.title: Plauchut, 1877
exploreItems.hint: Keep the source name, idea and limit together.
exploreItems.discovery: His account links lost exemptions with the uprising and describes expected support that did not arrive.

exploreItems.title: Izquierdo, 31 January 1872
exploreItems.hint: Keep the source name, idea and limit together.
exploreItems.discovery: His official report presents the suppression as stopping plans prepared in advance against Spanish rule.

exploreItems.title: Compare, do not jump
exploreItems.hint: Keep the source name, idea and limit together.
exploreItems.discovery: An account of a grievance or a wider plan does not by itself prove that the priests organized the event.

exploreItems.title: Clue 1
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Later writing: Rizal dedicated El Filibusterismo to the priests.

exploreItems.title: Clue 2
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Wider concern: remembrance connected the case with justice and the country.

exploreItems.title: Clue 3
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Limit: a dedication does not show everyone held the same view.

exploreItems.title: Foundation
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Rizal founded La Liga Filipina in Manila on 3 July 1892.

exploreItems.title: Shared purposes
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Its aims included unity, mutual protection, education, agriculture and commerce.

exploreItems.title: Interruption
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The association weakened after Rizal was arrested and sent to Dapitan.

exploreItems.title: First editor
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Graciano Lopez Jaena was the first editor of La Solidaridad.

exploreItems.title: Later editor
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Marcelo H. del Pilar later became its editor.

exploreItems.title: Writer
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Rizal contributed arguments for changes, including press freedom and representation.

exploreItems.title: Date and setting
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: La Solidaridad first appeared in 1889 in Spain.

exploreItems.title: Method
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Publication helped carry Philippine concerns and reform arguments to readers.

exploreItems.title: Limit
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Publication is a method of advocacy, not proof that a demand became law.

fields.title: Connections and Reform Evidence Challenge
fields.description: Complete 10 activities: five clue-and-conclusion decisions and five matching tasks. For each evidence decision, choose the lesson clue that answers the question, then choose the supported conclusion. Both parts count as one activity. Get at least 7 activities correct. You can use every supplied clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.question: Which lesson clue explains how Suez changed the Europe-Asia water connection?
fields.optionA: It offered a shorter water connection without removing travel costs.
fields.optionB: It guaranteed every family could afford travel.
fields.optionC: It stopped all movement of people and goods.
fields.optionD: It opened before the Iloilo port in 1855.

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The Suez clue identifies a shorter Europe-Asia water connection. A shorter route did not make travel free or equally available to everyone.
fields.learningPoint: The Suez clue identifies a shorter Europe-Asia water connection. A shorter route did not make travel free or equally available to everyone.
fields.historicalClue: The Suez clue identifies a shorter Europe-Asia water connection. A shorter route did not make travel free or equally available to everyone.

fields.question: Which clue directly supports the claim that the Malolos women took an educational initiative themselves?
fields.optionA: Rizal made the request for them before they took any action.
fields.optionB: A request proves every woman could already attend school.
fields.optionC: Their request was the founding of El Ilocano.
fields.optionD: The women requested a school and proposed their own funding.

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The dated request and proposed funding show the women taking initiative. The request came before Rizal's praise and is not proof of universal school access.
fields.learningPoint: The dated request and proposed funding show the women taking initiative. The request came before Rizal's praise and is not proof of universal school access.
fields.historicalClue: The dated request and proposed funding show the women taking initiative. The request came before Rizal's praise and is not proof of universal school access.

fields.question: Which clue explains secular clergy as an organization category, rather than having no religion?
fields.optionA: Secular identifies the nationality of every priest.
fields.optionB: Secular means a priest attends church less often.
fields.optionC: Secular clergy are under a bishop and are not members of a religious order.
fields.optionD: Secular means that a priest has no religious beliefs.

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: In this parish context, secular names a clergy category. It does not mean having no religion or establish nationality or personal worth.
fields.learningPoint: In this parish context, secular names a clergy category. It does not mean having no religion or establish nationality or personal worth.
fields.historicalClue: In this parish context, secular names a clergy category. It does not mean having no religion or establish nationality or personal worth.

fields.question: Which source clue connects lost exemptions with expected support that did not arrive?
fields.optionA: The clue alone proves the three priests organized the uprising.
fields.optionB: Plauchut's 1877 account includes both the reported grievance and failed support.
fields.optionC: Izquierdo wrote Plauchut's later account under another name.
fields.optionD: The clue proves no participant could have made any plan.

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The Plauchut clue includes lost exemptions and hoped-for support. A grievance does not rule out plans, and neither point alone proves the priests organized the event.
fields.learningPoint: The Plauchut clue includes lost exemptions and hoped-for support. A grievance does not rule out plans, and neither point alone proves the priests organized the event.
fields.historicalClue: The Plauchut clue includes lost exemptions and hoped-for support. A grievance does not rule out plans, and neither point alone proves the priests organized the event.

fields.question: Which clue identifies La Liga Filipina's shared aims rather than the work of a newspaper editor?
fields.optionA: The Liga aimed at unity, mutual protection, education, agriculture and commerce.
fields.optionB: The Liga was the first issue of La Solidaridad in 1889.
fields.optionC: The Liga was another name for the Spanish Cortes.
fields.optionD: Its aims prove every reform demand had already succeeded.

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The Liga was an association with shared aims. A newspaper editor has a different role, and a statement of aims is not evidence that every goal was achieved.
fields.learningPoint: The Liga was an association with shared aims. A newspaper editor has a different role, and a statement of aims is not evidence that every goal was achieved.
fields.historicalClue: The Liga was an association with shared aims. A newspaper editor has a different role, and a statement of aims is not evidence that every goal was achieved.
